communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Sheriff's Department PROTECT Act Policies November 2026 (Barnstable County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:
This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1. Sheriff’s Department policies, memos or other guidance  currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and a federal immigration authority, defined by M.G.L. Acts of 2026 C. 163 § 7 as “the United States Department of Homeland Security, United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, United States Customs and Border Protection or any successor entity, and any person acting on their behalf.” The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:
A. Fingerprint and other data sharing with the above-named federal entities,
B. Guidance or policies concerning when communication with federal immigration authorities is allowed. This includes policies concerning how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances. This also includes how and under what circumstances department employees are to document and respond to ICE detainer requests and other requests for information.

2. All Sheriff’s Department policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of sheriff department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies concerning the use of sheriff department parking lots, facility interior, or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.  

3. All training materials the Sheriff’s Department has developed, used or trained employees on from September 4, 2026 through October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026) regarding civil immigration enforcement, communication with federal immigration authorities, or the use of Sheriff’s department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. Citizens for Juvenile Justice is an independent nonprofit organization working to reform youth serving systems statewide through Massachusetts. We engage in advocacy across the Commonwealth to ensure all youth are treated fairly and equitably regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, disability or immigration status. We plan to use these records to ensure that all people in Massachusetts, including youth, are adequately protected by law enforcement agencies regardless of real or perceived immigration status.  In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.
The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,
Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initiatives 
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org

title: Deaths-in-custody

communications.subject: Hawaii Uniform Information Practices Act Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Hawaii Uniform Information Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

03/13/2025 

Andrew  Free 
MuckRock News, DEPT MR182997 
Boston, Massachusetts 02115 

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2025-ICFO-25070 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), dated 3/13/2025, your request for a waiver of all assessable FOIA fees, and your request for expedited treatment. Your request was received in this office on 3/13/2025. Specifically, you have requested records pertaining to a copy of the IHSC Mortality Review for Ousmane Ba, who died in ICE Custody February 23, 2024, according to the Detainee Death Report ICE published: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddr_OusmaneBa.pdf. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

ICE evaluates fee waiver requests under the legal standard set forth above and the fee waiver policy guidance issued by the Department of Justice on April 2, 1987, as incorporated into the Department of Homeland Security’s Freedom of Information Act regulations.  These regulations set forth six factors to examine in determining whether the applicable legal standard for fee waiver has been met.  I have considered the following factors in my evaluation of your request for a fee waiver: 

(1) Whether the subject of the requested records concerns “the operations or activities of the government”; 
(2) Whether the disclosure is “likely to contribute” to an understanding of government operations or activities; 
(3) Whether disclosure of the requested information will contribute to the understanding of the public at large, as opposed to the individual understanding of the requestor or a narrow segment of interested persons; 
(4) Whether the contribution to public understanding of government operations or activities will be "significant"; 
(5) Whether the requester has a commercial interest that would be furthered by the requested disclosure; and 
(6) Whether the magnitude of any identified commercial interest to the requestor is sufficiently large in comparison with the public interest in disclosure, that disclosure is primarily in the commercial interest of the requestor. 

Upon review of your request and a careful consideration of the factors listed above, I have determined to grant your request for a fee waiver. 

Your request for expedited treatment is hereby denied. 

Under the DHS FOIA regulations, expedited processing of a FOIA request is warranted if the request involves “circumstances in which the lack of expedited treatment could reasonably be expected to pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1)(i), or “an urgency to inform the public about an actual or alleged federal government activity, if made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(l)(ii).  Requesters seeking expedited processing must submit a statement explaining in detail the basis for the request, and that statement must be certified by the requester to be true and correct.  6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(3). 

Your request for expedited processing is denied because you do not qualify for either category under 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1).  You failed to demonstrate a particular urgency to inform the public about the government activity involved in the request beyond the public’s right to know about government activity generally.  Your letter was conclusory in nature and did not present any facts to justify a grant of expedited processing under the applicable standards. 

If you deem the decision to deny expedited treatment of your request an adverse determination, you have the right to appeal.  Should you wish to do so, you must send your appeal and a copy of this letter, within 90 days of the date of this letter following the procedures outlined in the DHS FOIA regulations at 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(e)(2). You may submit your appeal electronically at GILDFOIAAppeals@ice.dhs.gov or via regular mail to: 

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Office of the Principal Legal Advisor 
U.S. Department of Homeland Security 
500 12th Street,, S.W., Mail Stop 5900 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5900 

Your envelope and letter should be marked “FOIA Appeal.”  Copies of the FOIA and DHS regulations are available at www.dhs.gov/foia. 

ICE has queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions please contact FOIA Public Liaison Daniel Edgington, at (866) 633-1182 or 500 12th St, SW Stop 5009 Washington, DC 20536-5009. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2025-ICFO-25070. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2025-ICFO-25069 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), dated 3/13/2025, your request for a waiver of all assessable FOIA fees, and your request for expedited treatment. Your request was received in this office on 3/13/2025. Specifically, you have requested records pertaining to A copy of the IHSC Mortality Review for Charles Leo Daniel, who died in ICE Custody March 7, 2024, according to the Detainee Death Report ICE published: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddrDanielCharlesLeo.pdf.. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request. Per Section 5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt. Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period. As your request seeks numerous documents that will necessitate a thorough and wide-ranging search, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If you’re able to narrow the scope of your request please contact our office. Narrowing the scope may speed up the search process. We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

ICE evaluates fee waiver requests under the legal standard set forth above and the fee waiver policy guidance issued by the Department of Justice on April 2, 1987, as incorporated into the Department of Homeland Security’s Freedom of Information Act regulations.  These regulations set forth six factors to examine in determining whether the applicable legal standard for fee waiver has been met.  I have considered the following factors in my evaluation of your request for a fee waiver: 

(1) Whether the subject of the requested records concerns “the operations or activities of the government”; 
(2) Whether the disclosure is “likely to contribute” to an understanding of government operations or activities; 
(3) Whether disclosure of the requested information will contribute to the understanding of the public at large, as opposed to the individual understanding of the requestor or a narrow segment of interested persons; 
(4) Whether the contribution to public understanding of government operations or activities will be "significant"; 
(5) Whether the requester has a commercial interest that would be furthered by the requested disclosure; and 
(6) Whether the magnitude of any identified commercial interest to the requestor is sufficiently large in comparison with the public interest in disclosure, that disclosure is primarily in the commercial interest of the requestor. 

Upon review of your request and a careful consideration of the factors listed above, I have determined to grant your request for a fee waiver. 

Your request for expedited treatment is hereby denied. 

Under the DHS FOIA regulations, expedited processing of a FOIA request is warranted if the request involves “circumstances in which the lack of expedited treatment could reasonably be expected to pose an imminent threat to the life or physical safety of an individual,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1)(i), or “an urgency to inform the public about an actual or alleged federal government activity, if made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information,” 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(l)(ii).  Requesters seeking expedited processing must submit a statement explaining in detail the basis for the request, and that statement must be certified by the requester to be true and correct.  6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(3). 

Your request for expedited processing is denied because you do not qualify for either category under 6 C.F.R. § 5.5(e)(1).  You failed to demonstrate a particular urgency to inform the public about the government activity involved in the request beyond the public’s right to know about government activity generally.  Your letter was conclusory in nature and did not present any facts to justify a grant of expedited processing under the applicable standards. 

If you deem the decision to deny expedited treatment of your request an adverse determination, you have the right to appeal.  Should you wish to do so, you must send your appeal and a copy of this letter, within 90 days of the date of this letter following the procedures outlined in the DHS FOIA regulations at 6 C.F.R. Part 5 § 5.5(e)(2). You may submit your appeal electronically at GILDFOIAAppeals@ice.dhs.gov or via regular mail to: 

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Office of the Principal Legal Advisor 
U.S. Department of Homeland Security 
500 12th Street,, S.W., Mail Stop 5900 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5900 

Your envelope and letter should be marked “FOIA Appeal.”  Copies of the FOIA and DHS regulations are available at www.dhs.gov/foia. 

ICE has queried the appropriate program offices within ICE for responsive records. If any responsive records are located, they will be reviewed for determination of releasability. Please be assured that one of the processors in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions please contact FOIA Public Liaison Daniel Edgington, at (866) 633-1182 or 500 12th St, SW Stop 5009 Washington, DC 20536-5009. Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2025-ICFO-25069. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #2025-ICAP-00166
communications.communication:
Good morning, 

On May 22, 2025, the agency sent me a message stating "Subject: Re: Freedom of Information Act Request #2025-ICAP-0016
On April 22, 2025, final correspondence regarding this matter was sent to the email address on file."

That "final correspondence", in turn, contained an April 16 appeal decision affirming the agency's denial of expedited processing, but remanding "for the completion of processing, including tasking to the appropriate agency/office(s) to obtain any responsive
documents. The ICE FOIA Office will respond directly to you." 

I still have not received responsive records, a determination, or an estimated date of production. Does the agency intend to provide any of these statutorily required responses? If so, when? 

Thank you, 

Andrew Free

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Franklin Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Franklin Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

Thank you for providing the DCJIS/CJIS and CORI policy memos in response to our public records request. 

After reviewing the document, we would like to clarify the scope of our request concerning fingerprint and other data sharing. We understand that the policy addresses fingerprinting and background check requirements for employees, contractors, temporary staff, and other individuals with access to CJIS and FBI systems. 1. Fingerprinting and biometric data collection: Policies & procedures regarding the collection of fingerprints and other biometric data from individuals who are arrested, detained, or otherwise processed by the department. 2. Submission and dissemination of fingerprint & biometric data: Policies & procedures regarding what information collected from arrestees or detainees is submitted to or shared with: 

A. The Massachusetts State Police and other state agencies or databases
B. Federal agencies, including but not limited to the FBI, DHS, and ICE

3. Information shared with state and federal authorities: Policies & procedures regarding what type of information is shared with state and federal authorities including but not limited to fingerprints/biometric data, photographs, booking information, arrest records, charges, identifying information, and immigration status. 

If the department does not maintain records related to any of these categories, please let us know. If any of the requested information is already addressed in policies or procedures provided, we would appreciate identification of the relevant sections.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Sincerely,
Bernard Lin

title: Surveillance Cameras / ALPR Systems (Flock Safety) – Town of Fishkill

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: FOIL Request – Surveillance Cameras / ALPR Systems (Flock Safety) – Town of Fishkill
communications.communication:
Dear Records Custodian,

Under the provisions of the New York Freedom of Information Law (FOIL), N.Y. Public Officers Law §§ 84–90, I hereby request access to and copies of records held by the Town of Fishkill, Dutchess County, relating to the planning, proposal, procurement, authorization, or attempted deployment of Flock Safety surveillance cameras or automated license plate reader (ALPR) systems.

This request is made in the public interest to better understand the use, consideration, or implementation of surveillance technologies by local government entities, including decision-making processes, vendor relationships, and potential impacts on public privacy.

The purpose of this request is to determine the origin, authorization process, procurement activity, proposed locations, and communications surrounding any surveillance camera system, including identifying which individual, agency, or vendor first initiated discussions or planning for such a program within the Town of Fishkill.

Timeframe: January 1, 2023 – Present, including any earlier records referencing or relating to Flock Safety, automated license plate readers, or surveillance cameras within the Town of Fishkill.

Records Requested

For the purpose of this request, the records I seek include, but are not limited to the following:

1. Contracts and Agreements

All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, purchase orders, vendor agreements, procurement documents, or proposals involving the Town of Fishkill and Flock Safety or any related entities concerning surveillance cameras, automated license plate readers, or related monitoring technology.

This includes draft contracts, executed agreements, amendments, pilot program agreements, trial program documentation, cancellation notices, procurement justifications, and contract termination records.

Legal Basis: Contracts involving public funds or public infrastructure are public records subject to disclosure under N.Y. Public Officers Law § 87.

2. Records Identifying Project Initiation

All records reflecting the initial introduction, proposal, solicitation, or outreach regarding Flock Safety cameras or ALPR systems, including records identifying:

• the individual or office that first proposed or recommended the system  
• the first communications between the Town and Flock Safety  
• vendor outreach to town officials  
• internal discussions about introducing the technology  
• marketing or sales outreach from vendors  

3. Internal Communications

All internal communications including emails, memoranda, text messages, chat messages, letters, meeting notes, or other correspondence among:

• the Town Supervisor  
• Town Board members  
• Town of Fishkill Police Department personnel  
• Town administrative staff  
• Town legal counsel  
• Highway or Building Department personnel  
• other municipal offices  

that discuss:

• Flock Safety  
• automated license plate readers  
• surveillance cameras  
• camera deployments  
• vendor procurement or negotiations  
• surveillance technology adoption  

4. Communications With External Entities

All communications between the Town of Fishkill and:

• representatives of Flock Safety  
• technology vendors or consultants  
• Dutchess County officials  
• local, state, or federal law enforcement agencies  
• regional intelligence or real-time crime centers  

concerning surveillance cameras, ALPR systems, or the Flock Safety program.

5. Vendor Demonstrations and Sales Outreach

All records relating to vendor presentations, product demonstrations, marketing materials, or sales outreach regarding Flock Safety or related surveillance technology, including:

• presentation decks  
• vendor proposals  
• demonstration scheduling emails  
• meeting invitations or call summaries  
• webinar invitations  
• follow-up communications  

6. Proposed Camera Locations and Site Selection

All records identifying, evaluating, or discussing proposed or potential locations for surveillance cameras or automated license plate reader systems within the Town of Fishkill.

This includes but is not limited to:

• maps showing proposed camera placements  
• GIS maps or infrastructure maps  
• deployment plans  
• proposed installation locations or intersections  
• roadway monitoring points  
• entry or exit routes to the town  
• communications discussing site selection  
• vendor recommendations for placement  
• field surveys or site inspections  
• infrastructure or engineering assessments related to camera placement  

7. Deployment and Planning Documents

All planning or operational records relating to the surveillance system, including:

• deployment plans  
• camera location maps  
• infrastructure assessments  
• equipment specifications  
• installation schedules  
• operational capability descriptions  
• technology architecture documents  

8. Financial and Procurement Records

All records relating to funding, budgeting, or procurement of the surveillance system, including:

• invoices  
• payment records  
• purchase authorizations  
• budget allocations  
• grant applications  
• cost analyses  
• procurement justifications  
• financial approvals  

9. Meeting Records

All agendas, minutes, recordings, transcripts, or notes from Town Board meetings, committee meetings, departmental meetings, or internal meetings where surveillance camera programs or Flock Safety systems were discussed, proposed, approved, or canceled.

10. Oversight, Audit, and Compliance Records

Any audit reports, legal opinions, compliance reviews, investigations, or internal analyses relating to surveillance camera programs or procurement processes.

11. Data Access, Sharing, and Integration

All records relating to data access or sharing involving the surveillance system, including:

• agreements allowing other agencies to access camera data  
• policies governing license plate reader searches  
• records concerning integration with regional surveillance networks  
• data retention policies  
• privacy or civil liberties assessments  

Electronic Records and Metadata

For all responsive electronic records, including emails and digital documents, I request that records be produced in their native electronic format where possible, including all available metadata and email header information.

This includes, but is not limited to:

• sender and recipient information  
• CC and BCC fields  
• full email header routing data  
• timestamps for sending and receipt  
• message ID fields  
• attachment metadata  
• document creation dates  
• last modified dates  
• author fields  
• file path information where available  

Providing metadata is necessary to determine the origin, timing, and authorship of communications relating to the surveillance camera proposal.

Request for Segregable Non-Exempt Portions

Should any portion of the requested records be deemed exempt from disclosure, I request the release of any reasonably segregable non-exempt portions in accordance with N.Y. Public Officers Law § 87(2).

Preservation of Records

Please note your obligation not to destroy or alter any records potentially responsive to this request. Once a FOIL request has been received, agencies are required to preserve all responsive records during processing.

Fee Waiver Request

I request a fee waiver for the processing of this request as the information sought is in the public interest and its disclosure will contribute significantly to public understanding of government surveillance programs and decision-making processes.

If potential fees exceed $200, please inform me before proceeding.

Public Availability of Communications

Please be advised that communications relating to this request, including incoming and outgoing correspondence, may be publicly published on transparency platforms such as MuckRock.com.

Statutory Response Time

As required under N.Y. Public Officers Law § 89(3), I look forward to acknowledgment of this request within five business days.

Sincerely,

Jordan Lassiter  
Independent Investigative Journalist

communications.subject: FOIA request 1411473(Redex Corp)
communications.communication:
Good morning Ms. Best,

We're contacting you about the FOIA request you made for records concerning Redex Corp. The FBI has located approximately 2948 pages that are potentially responsive to your request. Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system, and the FBI receives a voluminous amount of requests on a daily, weekly, monthly, and annual basis.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium (51-950 pages), large (951-8000 pages), and extra-large (over 8000 pages) sub-tracks based upon request size. 

Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  The more potentially responsive pages a request has, the more complex it becomes, greatly increasing the time required for processing.  Generally, the larger the file, the longer it takes to process. A review of your request determined that it is currently in the complex request large processing track.  Given our current workload and staffing levels, it may yet be a long time before you begin to receive material from this request.   

Reducing the scope of your request may accelerate the processing and allow for a more timely receipt of the information you seek, as it could potentially place your request into a smaller, faster processing track.  This may also reduce duplication costs, if applicable.  Would you be willing to consider reducing the scope of your request?  If so, I would be happy to help you to decide the best approach to take.  We could potentially narrow your request by date, or if you are looking for something specific, we could approach the scope reduction process in that way.

Please let us know if you would like to potentially reduce the scope of your request.  We can be reached via email at fbi.foipa.negotiation@fbi.gov, or you may call 540-868-1695, Monday - Friday between the hours of 7:00am and 3:00pm Eastern time.

Best regards,

This may also reduce duplication costs, if applicable.  Would you be willing to consider reducing the scope of your request?  If so, we would be happy to help you to decide the best approach to take.  If you are looking for something specific, we could approach the scope reduction process in that way.

The current average time to complete a large track request is approximately 56 months. 

Please let us know if you would like to potentially reduce the scope of your request.  If you reduce the size, you can request the additional records with a new FOIA request upon completion of this one.

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: FOIA Request — RFP #23.09 Strategic Plan Facilitator: proposals, evaluation scores and contract

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA Request — RFP #23.09 Strategic Plan Facilitator: proposals, evaluation scores and contract
communications.communication:
Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Michigan Freedom of Information Act (MCL 15.231 et seq.), I request copies of the following records relating to Rochester Community Schools RFP #23.09, "Strategic Plan Facilitator" (2023; awarded to G&D Associates). The date range for this request is January 1, 2023 through September 30, 2026.

In this request, a reference to any record includes that record under any title the District uses for it; where a title differs, I request the record that serves that function.

1. The complete solicitation document for RFP #23.09, including all addenda and the evaluation criteria and weights.
2. The tabulation or summary of all proposals received (also called a bid abstract or proposal register), showing all proposers and all proposed prices, in its native spreadsheet format if maintained as one.
3. All evaluation and scoring records, including scoring sheets (also called evaluation forms, rating sheets, or scorecards), individual and consensus scores, rubrics, evaluator comments and worksheets (also called committee notes), and any interview or presentation scores. This includes evaluation records maintained in any e-procurement or agenda-management system the District uses.
4. All proposals submitted in response to RFP #23.09, including technical and cost proposals. If the volume is large, I prioritize: (a) the proposal of G&D Associates, and (b) the proposal of FourPoint Education Partners.
5. The executed contract (also called the agreement or professional services agreement) with G&D Associates, including scope of work, final price, term, and renewal options, plus all amendments, change orders, and extensions.
6. The board agenda item and supporting materials approving this award, including the funding source.
7. Line-item invoices submitted by, and payments (also called payment records or disbursement records) made to, G&D Associates under this contract, from the contract start through September 30, 2026.
8. The final deliverable(s) (also called work products or final reports) produced under this contract, including the adopted strategic plan document.

Please provide records in electronic format (searchable PDF or native files) where available, and produce records on a rolling basis as they are located and reviewed, beginning with the tabulation, scoring records, and executed contract, rather than holding all records until the full set is complete. If a responsive record is held by a third-party portal or vendor on the District's behalf, please produce it or identify where it is publicly posted. If any portion is withheld or redacted, please cite the specific statutory exemption and release all reasonably segregable portions. Pursuant to MCL 15.234, please provide an itemized fee estimate if fees will exceed $50, and contact me before processing if fees are expected to exceed $50; I do not authorize fees above $50 without my prior written approval.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Felipe Acano

title: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Clover Park School District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

title: DEA Records Concerning Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC) Credentials, Access, and Federal Participation

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: DEA Records Concerning Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC) Credentials, Access, and Federal Participation
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request the following records maintained by the Drug Enforcement Administration concerning Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC) events held at the Las Vegas Motor Speedway from January 1, 2023, through the date searches are conducted.

Specifically, I request:

Records reflecting the purchase, reimbursement, issuance, distribution, receipt, use, or acquisition of EDC admission credentials, tickets, VIP passes, hospitality credentials, media credentials, artist credentials, parking passes, backstage passes, or other event access credentials by or for DEA personnel.
Records reflecting requests made by DEA personnel to event organizers, promoters, contractors, or security providers for admission credentials, law-enforcement credentials, operational access, backstage access, VIP access, parking privileges, or other forms of event access.

Procurement records, purchase card records, reimbursement requests, travel vouchers, expense reports, invoices, receipts, or financial records relating to EDC admission credentials or event access.
Communications between DEA personnel and representatives of EDC, including but not limited to representatives of Insomniac Events, concerning credentials, operational access, law-enforcement support, intelligence gathering, interdiction activities, staffing, security coordination, or event participation.

Records sufficient to identify the number of DEA personnel assigned, deployed, credentialed, or granted access to EDC for each event year requested.

Calendars, briefing materials, meeting invitations, operational summaries, after-action reports, and executive briefings discussing DEA participation in EDC.

Communications between DEA Headquarters, the Los Angeles Field Division, and the Las Vegas District Office concerning EDC planning, staffing, credential requests, expenditures, intelligence support, or operational activities.

Records sufficient to identify overtime expenditures, travel expenditures, lodging expenditures, per diem payments, procurement expenditures, or other federal resources committed to EDC-related operations.

Any memoranda of understanding, operational agreements, coordination plans, or similar records concerning DEA participation in EDC-related activities.

Records sufficient to identify whether DEA personnel attended EDC in an official capacity, whether operational or observational, and the purpose of such attendance.

This request is not intended to seek information concerning private attendees or individual ticket purchasers. Rather, it seeks records concerning government operations, expenditures, staffing, access, and participation by DEA personnel.

For any records withheld in whole or in part, please provide a Vaughn index describing the basis for each withholding and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions.

Searches should include, at a minimum, DEA Headquarters, the Los Angeles Field Division, the Las Vegas District Office, email systems, Microsoft Teams communications, shared drives, calendars, expense systems, procurement systems, briefing repositories, and operational files reasonably likely to contain responsive records.

Fee Waiver Request

I request a waiver of all search, review, and duplication fees because disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest and is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of federal law-enforcement activities and expenditures at one of the largest music festivals in the United States. The requested records concern government operations and the use of public resources and are not sought for commercial purposes.

The information obtained will be analyzed and disseminated to the public through open-government and news-reporting activities.

If fees are expected to exceed $25, please notify me before processing.

I request the records in electronic format whenever possible.

Respectfully,

William Fernandes

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Fernandes

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #26-06467-F
communications.communication:
U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE
OFFICE OF INFORMATION POLICY
441 G Street, NW, 6th Floor
Washington, D.C. 20530
FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT ADMINISTRATIVE APPEAL
Appellant: William Fernandes
Agency: Drug Enforcement Administration
DEA FOIA Request No.: 25-07867-F

ADMINISTRATIVE APPEAL
To the Director:
Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, and the Department of Justice implementing regulations, Appellant respectfully submits this Administrative Appeal requesting reversal or remand of the Drug Enforcement Administration's determination.
This appeal concerns whether DEA has satisfied its statutory burden of conducting a search reasonably calculated to locate all responsive records and whether the administrative record demonstrates compliance with the Department's legal and ethical obligations in administering the Freedom of Information Act.
I. INTRODUCTION
Congress enacted the Freedom of Information Act to promote transparency, accountability, and public confidence in Government.
The Department of Justice has adopted the Standards of Ethical Conduct applicable to its employees, including the obligation that employees "shall put forth honest effort in the performance of their duties" and "shall endeavor to avoid any actions creating the appearance that they are violating the law or the ethical standards set forth in this part." 5 C.F.R. § 2635.101(b)(5) & (14).
Those principles are particularly important in the administration of FOIA because requesters, reviewing authorities, and ultimately the public must necessarily rely upon the accuracy and completeness of agency representations describing searches performed outside public view.
II. BACKGROUND
The subject of this request concerns Electric Daisy Carnival ("EDC"), one of the largest and longest-running electronic music festivals in the United States. Having existed for more than thirty years and attracting hundreds of thousands of attendees annually, EDC has generated substantial law enforcement interest and interagency coordination over many years.
Given the event's longevity, national prominence, and recurring operational significance, it is reasonable to expect that responsive records have accumulated throughout numerous DEA offices, custodians, intelligence products, operational files, correspondence, planning documents, after-action reports, archived records, electronic communications, and historical record systems.
The longevity and prominence of the subject substantially increase the likelihood that responsive records exist in multiple repositories, making a narrowly focused search insufficient to satisfy the requirements of 5 U.S.C. § 552.
III. THIS APPEAL CONCERNS A RECURRING ADMINISTRATIVE DEFICIENCY
The administrative record in this matter cannot reasonably be viewed in isolation.
Appellant's experience with this DEA FOIA office over numerous requests and administrative appeals reflects a recurring pattern in which initial determinations have required appellate intervention before the agency fulfilled its statutory obligations. The purpose of review by the Office of Information Policy is not merely to correct isolated administrative mistakes, but to identify recurring deficiencies that undermine public confidence in the Department's administration of the Freedom of Information Act.
Where repeated remands become necessary before an agency performs searches reasonably calculated to locate responsive records, OIP should determine whether the issue extends beyond an individual request and reflects broader deficiencies in search methodology, supervisory review, quality control, training, or compliance with Department policy.
This appeal therefore requests not only review of the present determination but careful examination of whether the administrative practices employed by this FOIA office continue to satisfy the standards expected by the Department of Justice.

IV. THE FBI'S RESPONSIVE RECORDS FURTHER HIGHLIGHT THE NEED FOR REVIEW
Appellant submitted a substantially similar request to the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

The FBI has advised Appellant that it identified responsive records FOIA Number: 1671779-000 and is presently processing those records for release.
Appellant fully recognizes that different Department of Justice components maintain different records.
However, when one DOJ component identifies a body of responsive records concerning substantially similar subject matter while another component reports dramatically different results, the disparity warrants careful administrative scrutiny.
This comparison does not establish that DEA necessarily possesses identical records.
It does, however, raise legitimate questions concerning whether DEA searched every office, custodian, archive, repository, and electronic records system reasonably likely to contain responsive information.
V. POLLING REQUESTS ARE AN IMPORTANT ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISM
Appellant routinely submits corresponding requests to multiple agencies and Department components addressing the same factual subject.
These parallel requests serve an important oversight function.
Comparison of agency responses frequently identifies:
omitted custodians;
incomplete search methodologies;
overlooked repositories;
inconsistent interpretations of identical requests;
failures to refer records;
administrative deficiencies requiring corrective action.
Such requests strengthen—not burden—the administration of FOIA by allowing independent comparison of agency search efforts.
Indeed, Appellant's prior administrative appeals involving DEA have resulted in remands requiring additional processing after OIP determined that further administrative action was warranted. Those prior remands demonstrate the continuing importance of meaningful appellate review where legitimate questions exist concerning the adequacy of an agency's search.
VI. DEA HAS NOT MET ITS BURDEN
DEA bears the burden of demonstrating that it conducted a search reasonably calculated to locate all responsive records.
The present administrative record does not establish whether DEA searched:
Microsoft Outlook email;
Microsoft Teams communications;
archived mailboxes;
text messages;
government-issued mobile devices;
intelligence repositories;
shared drives;
historical archives;
supervisory correspondence;
operational planning files;
after-action reports;
legacy record systems;
referrals received from other Department of Justice components.
Absent such information, neither Appellant nor OIP can meaningfully evaluate whether DEA has discharged its statutory obligations.
VII. DUTY OF CANDOR
The Freedom of Information Act depends upon accurate factual representations regarding agency search efforts.
This appeal does not merely challenge DEA's conclusions.
It challenges whether the administrative record sufficiently demonstrates that DEA exercised the diligence required by law.
When significant questions remain concerning the scope of a search, the custodians contacted, the repositories examined, or the methodology employed, independent appellate review becomes essential to preserving confidence in the Department's FOIA process.
VIII. THE DEPARTMENT'S OWN ETHICAL STANDARDS SUPPORT REMAND
The Department of Justice requires its employees to conduct themselves in a manner that preserves public confidence in Government.
Employees are required to put forth honest effort in the performance of their duties and to endeavor to avoid actions creating the appearance that they are violating the law or applicable ethical standards.
Those principles reinforce—not replace—the statutory requirements imposed by FOIA.
Where the administrative record leaves substantial unanswered questions concerning the adequacy of an agency's search, the Department's own ethical standards support independent review to ensure that statutory obligations have been fully satisfied.
IX. REQUEST FOR RELIEF
Appellant respectfully requests that the Office of Information Policy:
Reverse or remand DEA's determination.
Direct DEA to conduct a new search reasonably calculated to locate all responsive records.
Require DEA to identify every custodian, office, and repository searched.
Require DEA to disclose the search terms employed.
Require DEA to explain the substantial disparity between its search results and those identified by another Department of Justice component processing substantially similar subject matter.
Require DEA to submit a supplemental declaration describing its search methodology in reasonable detail.
Direct release of all reasonably segregable portions of responsive records.
Grant such additional relief as OIP deems just and appropriate under the Freedom of Information Act.
Respectfully submitted,
/s/
William Fernandes

Also note that the DEA office assigned the FOIA number 26-06467-F on June 14, 2026 use of -F is usually an obstruction or instant denial indicator to best of my knowledge.
