communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #26-06467-F
communications.communication:
Sent via DOJ Portal 10/08/26 by William

October 8, 2026
Director
Office of Information Policy
U.S. Department of Justice
441 G Street, NW, Sixth Floor
Washington, DC 20530
RE: FORMAL REQUEST FOR RECONSIDERATION, SUPERVISORY REVIEW, AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
Administrative Appeal No. A-2026-01955
DEA FOIA Request No. 26-06467-F
OIP Determination Dated September 29, 2026
Subject: Improper Whole-Request Rejection, Failure to Consider Partial Processing, Unsubstantiated Search Burden, and Concerns Regarding Administrative Impartiality
Dear Director:
I formally challenge the September 29, 2026 determination issued by Rianna Barrett, Associate Chief, Administrative Appeals Staff, affirming the Drug Enforcement Administration's rejection of FOIA Request No. 26-06467-F concerning records associated with the Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC), DEA employee participation, and DEA operations connected with the event.
I request reconsideration of this determination, supervisory review of the agency's reasonable-description analysis, and corrective action to facilitate the identification, processing, and disclosure of responsive records.
The determination appears to adopt an unnecessarily expansive characterization of the administrative burden associated with my request while failing to meaningfully consider DEA's established organizational structure, readily identifiable geographic jurisdictions, limited operational groups, centralized records repositories, and the possibility of separately processing sufficiently described categories of information.
The handling of this matter also raises legitimate concerns regarding administrative professionalism, impartiality, and the unnecessary expenditure of requester and government resources in resolving issues that could be addressed through established FOIA processing procedures.
I. IMPROPER WHOLE-REQUEST REJECTION AND FAILURE TO CONSIDER PARTIAL PROCESSING
OIP affirmed DEA's determination that the request was insufficiently described under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(3)(A) and 28 C.F.R. § 16.3(b).
The determination suggests that DEA would be required to search thousands of employee email accounts or undertake extensive research to identify personnel who may have participated in EDC.
This explanation fails to meaningfully distinguish among the separate categories of information identified in the request.
Federal agencies routinely issue partial grants and partial denials under FOIA. The statute contemplates individualized disclosure determinations, including the release of reasonably segregable nonexempt information.
Although the reasonable-description requirement must be satisfied before an agency is obligated to conduct a search, sufficiently identifiable portions of a request should receive appropriate consideration even where other portions require clarification.
The question is whether DEA evaluated the separately identifiable records categories before determining that the entire request could not reasonably be processed.
The determination does not document such an evaluation.
Records concerning DEA operational activity at a specific public event may be maintained in entirely different systems from records identifying individual employees who attended an event in a personal capacity.
These differences matter.
A centralized event-operation file, task-force coordination memorandum, supervisory communication, or administrative authorization may be reasonably identifiable without establishing the identity of every DEA employee who attended the event.
I request that OIP reconsider its blanket affirmation and direct DEA to evaluate whether independently identifiable categories of responsive records may be processed.
II. DEA'S NATIONAL WORKFORCE SIZE IS NOT A REASONABLE SUBSTITUTE FOR IDENTIFYING APPROPRIATE RECORDS CUSTODIANS
OIP's determination relies upon a generalized assertion that DEA would need to search thousands of employee email accounts.
That premise appears disconnected from the agency's actual organizational structure and the geographically limited subject matter of the request.
DEA's former Administrator, Anne Milgram, described the agency as employing nearly 10,000 personnel in congressional testimony dated July 27, 2023.
Regardless of whether the agency's total present workforce is closer to 10,000 or 12,500 personnel, its nationwide staffing complement provides little meaningful information concerning the effort necessary to identify records associated with a particular event in Las Vegas.
The relevant inquiry concerns the organizational units reasonably likely to maintain responsive records.
DEA's January 26, 2026 announcement appointing Anthony Chrysanthis as Special Agent in Charge of the Los Angeles Field Division expressly identifies Nevada among the jurisdictions supervised by that division.
Las Vegas therefore falls within the established regional organizational structure of DEA's Los Angeles Field Division.
This information is publicly available on DEA's own website.
It provides an identifiable starting point for determining which organizational units may maintain records associated with the requested activities.
Rather than presuming that thousands of unrelated individual employee accounts require examination, DEA could assess whether responsive records are maintained by:
1.	The DEA Las Vegas office and its relevant supervisory personnel.
2.	The Los Angeles Field Division and appropriate regional management offices.
3.	Any DEA operational group or task force assigned responsibilities associated with EDC.
4.	Personnel responsible for interagency event coordination or operational planning.
5.	Centralized operational, administrative, or correspondence systems reasonably likely to contain event-related records.
6.	Any designated operational coordinator, group supervisor, or administrative office responsible for maintaining activity records.
These are potential search locations requiring agency evaluation. Their identification does not presume that responsive records necessarily exist.
Nevertheless, the existence of DEA's established geographic hierarchy materially undermines an unexplained assertion that the request necessarily requires an agency-wide examination of individual employee accounts.
III. LIMITED TASK-FORCE STAFFING AND THE POSSIBILITY OF A NARROWLY TARGETED SEARCH
The agency's characterization also overlooks the possibility that any relevant operational activity associated with EDC would have been coordinated through a comparatively small group of personnel.
A geographically limited DEA operational group or task force might involve fewer than 100 personnel, potentially substantially fewer.
This figure is offered as an estimate for purposes of evaluating search methodology. DEA possesses the staffing, assignment, and organizational information necessary to establish the actual complement of any relevant unit.
The reasonable-description analysis should consider whether records could be identified through a limited number of supervisory or operational custodians rather than thousands of unrelated employees.
For example, a particular operational assignment might generate administrative communications, coordination records, reports, approvals, or activity documentation maintained within the responsible unit.
Such records would not necessarily require individual examination of every employee's email account.
OIP has not explained whether the Las Vegas office, the Los Angeles Field Division, or any potentially relevant task-force component was consulted regarding the existence or organization of responsive records.
Nor has OIP explained whether DEA attempted to identify the appropriate organizational component before concluding that a reasonable search could not be conducted.
I request reconsideration based upon a meaningful assessment of the actual administrative structures through which responsive records might be located.
IV. FAILURE TO ADEQUATELY APPLY 28 C.F.R. § 16.3(b)
DOJ's regulation at 28 C.F.R. § 16.3(b) provides the governing standard for reasonably describing requested records.
The regulation requires a description sufficient to enable agency personnel to locate records with a reasonable amount of effort.
Where an agency determines that a request does not reasonably describe the records sought, the regulation requires the agency to inform the requester what additional information is needed or explain why the request is otherwise insufficient.
The regulation also provides for assistance through agency FOIA personnel, the FOIA Public Liaison, and OIP.
OIP's September 29 determination affirms DEA's position and refers me to the DEA FOIA Public Liaison.
However, the determination does not meaningfully explain why DEA could not assess the readily identifiable regional and operational records repositories before concluding that the request was insufficiently described in its entirety.
An appropriate reasonable-description assessment should reflect the agency's actual records-management practices.
If DEA requires a particular date range, record category, custodian designation, organizational unit, or other identifying information, it should state precisely what is necessary.
A generalized characterization of the request as broad or sweeping does not explain whether sufficiently described portions can be processed.
I request that OIP direct DEA to identify the specific deficiencies associated with each disputed records category and provide actionable clarification requirements.
V. DOJ'S OWN PUBLISHED GUIDANCE FAVORS FAIR INTERPRETATION OF REQUESTS
OIP's published guidance, "Determining the Scope of a FOIA Request," emphasizes the importance of fairly interpreting the language of FOIA requests and avoiding unnecessarily restrictive constructions.
The guidance discusses Hemenway v. Hughes, 601 F. Supp. 1002, 1005 (D.D.C. 1985), and the importance of interpreting requests in a manner consistent with identifying responsive records.
The reasonable-description requirement serves a practical purpose: enabling agencies to locate records using reasonable effort.
It should not be administered through hypothetical search assumptions divorced from the agency's actual organization.
Federal agencies possess institutional knowledge regarding their records systems, supervisory assignments, filing practices, and organizational responsibilities that requesters generally cannot access.
This imbalance is particularly important where the requested information concerns internal law-enforcement operations or employee assignments.
DEA knows which components exercise jurisdiction over Las Vegas, which offices coordinate local activities, and which records systems are ordinarily used by those components.
A requester should not be required to identify every internal filing system or individual custodian before the agency meaningfully evaluates whether the requested records can reasonably be located.
I request that OIP apply its own published guidance in reviewing DEA's interpretation of the request.
VI. DISTINCTION BETWEEN REASONABLE SEARCH REQUIREMENTS AND EXHAUSTIVE INVESTIGATION
A FOIA search must be reasonably calculated to uncover responsive records. It does not ordinarily require an agency to examine every conceivable location or undertake unlimited investigative research.
That principle is relevant to DEA's burden analysis.
OIP's determination suggests that DEA would need to research which of its thousands of employees attended EDC.
That may describe one conceivable approach to an employee-participation inquiry.
It does not demonstrate that the same methodology would be necessary to identify operational records concerning the event.
A reasonable agency search may begin with the offices, custodians, or records systems most likely to contain the requested material.
DEA's identified regional structure offers practical opportunities for such an assessment.
The decision should explain why these more targeted approaches would not resolve at least portions of the request.
An assertion that an unnecessarily broad search would be burdensome does not independently establish that a narrower, organizationally appropriate search is unavailable.
VII. PARTIAL GRANTS, PARTIAL DENIALS, AND RECORDS SEGREGABILITY
FOIA permits different dispositions for separately identified categories of records.
An agency may release some responsive records, withhold others under applicable statutory exemptions, or determine that no records were located following an adequate search.
Under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8), the agency must also consider applicable requirements concerning foreseeable harm and segregability when withholding responsive information.
These disclosure provisions do not eliminate the threshold reasonable-description requirement.
They nevertheless demonstrate that the statutory scheme recognizes differentiated treatment of records rather than unnecessarily categorical disposition.
OIP should evaluate whether the original submission included discrete, sufficiently described categories that could be processed without first resolving every issue concerning other categories.
For example, a request for operational coordination records may present materially different search considerations from a request requiring identification of all employees who personally attended a public event.
The two inquiries should not automatically be treated as administratively inseparable.
I request appropriate partial processing of any categories that independently satisfy FOIA's reasonable-description standard.
VIII. FAILURE TO ESTABLISH THE FACTUAL BASIS FOR THE CLAIMED SEARCH BURDEN
OIP's determination does not identify the factual or organizational basis for DEA's claim that thousands of email accounts would require examination.
It does not identify the components consulted, the categories of records reviewed for search feasibility, or the regional offices considered.
It provides no explanation of whether DEA evaluated centralized operational or supervisory records.
Nor does it establish that potentially responsive material could only be retrieved through individual employee-level searches.
I request that OIP obtain a substantive explanation addressing the following matters:
1.	Whether DEA consulted its Las Vegas office regarding the request.
2.	Whether the Los Angeles Field Division was consulted or identified as a potential records custodian.
3.	Whether any task-force, operational, or supervisory group was evaluated as a potential records repository.
4.	Whether records concerning event planning, operational authorization, coordination, or related administrative activities could be identified through centralized systems.
5.	The factual basis for asserting that thousands of employee accounts would require examination.
6.	Whether separately identifiable portions of the request were evaluated for partial processing.
7.	Whether DEA considered clarification of specific categories rather than wholesale rejection.
8.	Whether any responsive records had already been identified or located during preliminary processing.
A meaningful response to these questions would assist in determining whether the agency's original position reflected actual records-management limitations or an unnecessarily expansive construction of the requested search.
IX. ADMINISTRATIVE IMPARTIALITY, PROFESSIONALISM, AND APPEARANCE OF IMPROPRIETY
I have successfully pursued hundreds of federal Freedom of Information Act and Privacy Act requests, including complex administrative appeals involving multiple Department of Justice components.
My experience includes the evaluation of agency search methodologies, disclosure requirements, records-management systems, exemption determinations, and procedural deficiencies.
I am familiar with the practical limitations of FOIA administration and the distinction between reasonable records searches and unduly burdensome investigative inquiries.
Against that background, I find the September 29 determination unnecessarily dismissive of the substantive issues presented.
The agency's characterization of the request as requiring examination of thousands of employee accounts, followed by the suggestion that I contact the DEA FOIA Public Liaison, fails to adequately engage with readily identifiable organizational alternatives.
This handling creates an appearance of discouragement toward a requester who has consistently exercised established statutory disclosure rights.
I am concerned that the disposition may reasonably be perceived as intimidating, harassing, or unnecessarily adversarial, particularly where the asserted burden has not been explained through reference to DEA's actual organizational structure.
I request an objective supervisory examination of whether the handling of this appeal reflects appropriate standards of impartiality, fairness, and professional conduct.
An adverse determination alone does not establish intentional harassment or retaliation. The concern here is the combination of unsupported search assumptions, inadequate consideration of alternatives, and the resulting administrative burden placed upon the requester.
Federal employees entrusted with the administration of disclosure rights should endeavor to avoid impropriety and the appearance of impropriety.
They should also avoid unnecessary procedural obstacles that may discourage lawful participation in government transparency processes.
The Office of Information Policy occupies a particularly important position in maintaining these standards throughout the Department of Justice.
I request that OIP ensure its personnel approach administrative appeals with appropriate independence, professionalism, and an objective commitment to lawful disclosure.
X. UNNECESSARY EXPENDITURE OF REQUESTER AND GOVERNMENT RESOURCES
The handling of this matter raises additional concerns regarding administrative efficiency.
The preparation of an administrative appeal, followed by further reconsideration correspondence, requires substantial time, research, and effort.
These expenditures can often be avoided through reasonable communication concerning records scope and appropriate search locations.
A targeted inquiry to the DEA Las Vegas office or Los Angeles Field Division may require substantially fewer resources than an agency-wide inquiry involving thousands of employees.
Likewise, specific clarification regarding a disputed records category may eliminate unnecessary disagreement without requiring supervisory intervention or judicial proceedings.
The prolonged expenditure of public and private resources to resolve a dispute concerning readily identifiable geographic jurisdiction appears inconsistent with efficient FOIA administration.
I request that OIP endeavor to minimize unnecessary administrative friction and direct its attention toward resolving the underlying disclosure issues.
The purpose of the FOIA process is to facilitate lawful public access to agency records through established procedures.
Its effectiveness should be measured by the adequacy of those procedures and their results rather than by the number of administrative obstacles imposed upon requesters.
XI. REQUEST FOR SUPERVISORY REVIEW AND CORRECTIVE ACTION
I respectfully request the following corrective measures:
1.	Reconsider and withdraw the September 29, 2026 determination affirming DEA's rejection of FOIA Request No. 26-06467-F.
2.	Remand the request for renewed consideration under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(3)(A) and 28 C.F.R. § 16.3(b).
3.	Require DEA to evaluate separately identifiable categories of requested records and process any portions that independently satisfy the reasonable-description requirement.
4.	Direct DEA to consider a geographically limited assessment involving the Las Vegas office and Los Angeles Field Division.
5.	Require consideration of appropriate operational, supervisory, task-force, and centralized administrative records systems.
6.	Obtain the factual basis for DEA's assertion that thousands of employee email accounts would require examination.
7.	Require specific clarification instructions for any portion of the request that DEA continues to regard as insufficiently described.
8.	Facilitate the processing and disclosure of responsive records located through reasonable searches, with individualized application of any legally justified exemptions.
9.	Conduct a supervisory review of the handling of this appeal, including the adequacy of the written determination and any appearance of unnecessarily adversarial or discouraging treatment.
10.	Provide a written response addressing the objections presented and identifying the corrective action adopted.
11.	Ensure that the original request, administrative appeal, related correspondence, and processing records are retained in accordance with applicable federal records-management requirements.
XII. PRESERVATION OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND JUDICIAL RIGHTS
The September 29 determination advises that the administrative appeal has been denied and expressly identifies the right to seek judicial review under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(B).
This correspondence seeks discretionary reconsideration and supervisory review of that determination.
I preserve all applicable administrative and judicial rights and remedies, including judicial review and assistance through the Office of Government Information Services.
This request for reconsideration should be addressed on its merits without prejudicing any previously accrued right to judicial review.
I further request preservation of records documenting the handling of the underlying FOIA request and appeal, including internal communications, processing notes, referrals, consultations, and materials relied upon in reaching the reasonable-description determination, subject to applicable records-retention obligations.
XIII. CONCLUSION
The September 29 determination rests upon an insufficiently explained assertion that processing my request would require examining thousands of DEA employee accounts.
That proposition deserves substantial scrutiny given DEA's established organizational structure, the Los Angeles Field Division's jurisdiction over Nevada, and the existence of identifiable regional and operational offices through which potentially responsive records may be maintained.
DEA's nationwide workforce size cannot substitute for a practical assessment of the records systems reasonably likely to contain information relevant to a specific public event in Las Vegas.
A hypothetical nationwide search should not displace consideration of geographically limited and organizationally appropriate alternatives.
The reasonable-description requirement should be applied constructively, with due regard for the agency's actual records-management practices and the independently identifiable categories of information requested.
I further request that OIP ensure its administrative personnel exercise appropriate impartiality, professionalism, and sound judgment when corresponding with experienced FOIA requesters.
The unnecessary expenditure of time and resources in avoidable administrative disputes undermines both the purpose of the Freedom of Information Act and the public's confidence in government records administration.
I request prompt supervisory intervention, reconsideration of the September 29 determination, and appropriate corrective action to advance the processing and disclosure of responsive agency records.
Respectfully,
/s/
William Fernandes
________________________________________

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Internal Complaints (2010 - Present) (Pierce County Sheriff's Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the period from January 1, 2010 to the date this request was filed, please provide a spreadsheet of all complaints against officers in CSV or Excel format with only the following columns: Investigation/Complaint No., Incident Type, Occurred Date, Complaint Reported On Date, Employee Badge Number, Employee First Name, Employee Last Name, Allegation, Allegation: Policy/Directive Violated, Allegation: Finding, Disposition, Discipline Imposed.

Please provide all complaints, regardless of severity,in cluding any complaints that may not have been classified for full investigation and were referred to an employee's supervisor for counseling or retraining as well as complaints that were investigated by an employee's command instead of the normal internal affairs process. I would ask that you fulfill my request in a single installment in one spreadsheet instead of splitting it up into multiple annual spreadsheets if possible.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Rose Terse

title: Jail booking fields and 30-day booking log (Chaffee County Sheriff)

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Jail booking fields and 30-day booking log (Chaffee County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
Hello, and thank you for the work you do at the Chaffee County Sheriff.

I'm writing from the Records Desk at Tempo by Multido with a small public records request under the Colorado Open Records Act (CORA) and Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act (CCJRA). I know records staff are busy, so I've tried to keep this as simple as I can.

Could you please share:

1. A list of the fields your jail booking system keeps (for example: booking number, booking date, name, date of birth, charges, bond, release date, booking photo). A screenshot, a report header or a short description is perfectly fine.
2. The booking log for the most recent 30 days, in whatever electronic form is easiest for you. A standard report export, a spreadsheet or a PDF all work.

I'd also love to know: does your office offer an email list, notification system or regular report (daily or weekly) that shares new bookings or arrests? If so, we'd be glad to sign up, so you wouldn't need to handle requests like this one in the future.

If any part is exempt, please feel free to send the rest. And if another office is the better place to ask, a quick pointer would be very much appreciated.

Thank you so much for your time and help. We really appreciate it.

Warmly,
Logan

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #2024-CRFO-00207
communications.communication:
Good afternoon, 

We received your response to our request yesterday. Thank you very much for providing it. We appeal the following aspects of this response: 

1. We appeal the adequacy of CRCL's search. 
The agency provided a 10-page document with several withholdings, and noted that an additional 66 pages were referred to ICE (63) and OIG (3). However, the records CRCL supplied demonstrate additional responsive records exist that an adequate search would have turned up, and that those records were not provided. First, there is a word document entitled "Complaint 005843-23-ICE Short Form.docx attached to the August 1, 2023 email at page 8 of the response that appears to be a CRCL document that is excluded from the agency's response. Second, there are two attachments to the August 3, 2023 email that appear to be CRCL documents and are not included. Third, there are appears to be an attachment to the October 13, 2023, email entitled "2023.08.29-[b6].pdf" that is not included in the production. Fourth, the October 13 email contains an apparent link to "Civil Liberties Collaboration Tool - 23-CRCL-4775 Dumitrascu, Cristian (SND) - All Documents (sharepoint.com). None of the CRCL documents from this Sharepoint drive, and no screenshots of the folder, appear in the CRCL production. For these reasons, CRCL's search appears to have overlooked obvious leads and the agency appears to have failed to undertake an iterative review of responsive materials in the initial production for potential additional responsive records. Our request sought [a]ny reports, investigative records, correspondence, taskings, notifications, or expert reviews by CRCL experts" in response to Mr. Dumitrascu's death. It does not appear from this 10-page document that the agency is provided all responsive records. 

2. We appeal the application of Exemption 5. 
Given the context of the released material, it is clear that exemption 5 does not apply to all of the redacted  portions because these are not interagency communications that are pre-decisional and deliberative in nature. Communications between a non-CRCL subject matter expert contractor (2024-CRFO-00207-000010) do not qualify for protection under Exemption 5 because they are not inter- or intra-agency communications within the definition of the contractor corollary as adopted by FOIA courts. The SME is independent, and thus, they are not being asked to perform a duty of a CRCL employee, but an outside contractor's function. Indeed--it is the SME consultant's independent and unbiased position separate and apart from the government structural that CRCL valued when it contracted with them. 

As to remaining exemption 5 applications, the materials redacted are not pre-decisional. Rather, they reflect the implementation of a decision already taken, i.e., to conduct a CRCL review of the death of Mr. Dumitrascu. 

3. We appeal the agency's application of Exemption 6. 
As to Exemption 6, the records CRCL do not meet the threshold for invoking the exemption. They are not medical files. They are not personnel files. And they are not similar to medical or personnel files. They are emails. Consequently, the Exemption 6 threshold is not met. Even if it were, however, we appeal the application of Exemption 6 to email domain names, which are block-redacted in the agency's production. 

4. We appeal the agency's failure to release all reasonably segregable nonexempt material.
As an initial matter, it appears from the first three pages of CRCL's response that the agency failed to release all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions of the pages the agency withheld in full (WIF) under exemptions 5 and 6. Even assuming exemption 5 could cover some of the information on this WIF pages, it cannot be applied to withhold factual information regarding Mr. Dumitrascu's death. See Transgender Law Center v. ICE, 46 F.3d 771, 785 (9th Cir. 2021).

5. We appeal the agency's redactions in full because CRCL made no foreseeable harm determination.
We appeal the application of Exemptions 5 and 6 because the agency has not asserted that any foreseeable harm will come from releasing any of the otherwise exempt material. Congress amended FOIA in 2016 to add the foreseeable harm standard, and require release of material that would be withheld unless an official within the agency determines such release would cause foreseeable harm. No such determination is possible on the basis of the records released. Indeed, it is the government's secrecy with respect to oversight about deaths in ICE custody that causes harm--not transparency about that process. 

For the above reasons, we appeal CRCL's May 28 FOIA response and request that the 10 pages be released in full, the unprovided attachments be provided, the Sharepoint drive be released to the extent it contains CRCL records, and all other responsive records that would be located through an iterative, adequate search be released. 

Thank you very much for your timely acknowledgement and response to this appeal. 

Andrew Free

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA Request – NCIS LInX/D-DEx Contract Records (Peraton IDV N0018922DZ036 and related orders)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The records are maintained by NAVSUP FLC Norfolk, Contracting Department, Philadelphia Office, which issued solicitation N0018922RZ004 and awarded IDV N0018922DZ036. I have filed an identical request with the Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS) so the offices can coordinate; please do not refer this request in a way that delays production.

1. Contract file, IDV N0018922DZ036 (Peraton Inc., LInX/D-DEx System Support, awarded Sept. 7, 2022). The base contract with all sections, attachments, and exhibits, including the Performance Work Statement or Statement of Work, the Contract Data Requirements List (DD Form 1423), the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan, and all modifications. Also the solicitation N0018922RZ004 and all amendments and attachments.

2. Task and delivery orders. For each order below, the order document, its PWS/SOW or task description, and all modifications:
- N0018926FW149 (FY26 LInX Data Integration Task Order – TO 29)
- N0018924FZ543 (LInX/D-DEx Integration Fees and Software)
- N0018922FZ649, N0018924FZ095, N0018924FZ299 (LInX/D-DEx System Support – Data Integration)
- Order 0017 under IDV N0018911DZ041 (Data Integration & Consolidation Support, 2014)
- Order 0001 under IDV N0018916DZ051 (NCIS Data Feeds, 2016)

3. Deliverables. For IDV N0018922DZ036 and the orders in Item 2, from Sept. 7, 2022 to the date of search: all monthly and periodic status reports; data source inventories; interface control documents; data feed lists; and agency onboarding or integration trackers.

4. Data sources. Records sufficient to identify every data source integrated or proposed for integration into LInX or D-DEx, by region, from January 1, 2012 to the date of search, including any automated license plate reader (ALPR/LPR) data source and any feed from Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions/Vigilant, Axon, ELSAG/Leonardo, Rekor, or any High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) program.

5. Privacy compliance. Any Privacy Impact Assessment for LInX or D-DEx, and any draft, revised, or proposed System of Records Notice for those systems prepared after May 6, 2010 (the date of SORN N05520-6 DoD, 75 FR 24931).

6. Invoices. Invoices with line-item (CLIN) detail for orders N0018926FW149 and N0018924FZ543.

Search terms. For Items 3 and 4, at minimum: "LPR," "ALPR," "license plate," "plate reader," "Flock," "Vigilant," "HIDTA," "Southeast," "LEAP," and "Dunwoody."

Segregability. I do not seek contractor unit pricing. If any portion of a record is withheld under any exemption, release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions as required by 5 U.S.C. § 552(b), and identify the specific exemption for each withholding. A list of the data sources feeding a system is not a law enforcement technique or procedure under Exemption 7(E). Contract documents and contractor deliverables are agency records regardless of the status of the underlying law enforcement data.

Format. Produce records electronically, in native format where available, on a rolling basis as they are processed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

communications.communication:

Ben Welsh

communications.communication:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025. If no database or spreadsheet format is available, please provide copies of each individual use of force report or other report where use of force information is documented/reported by officers. Note, this is for all use of force incidents reported by your agency, not limited to only those incidents required to be reported under state or federal programs.

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: DeFlock fusion center records (San Diego Law Enforcement Coordination Center)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Public reporting indicates that law-enforcement fusion centers have monitored the "DeFlock" movement, including reporting described at https://danboguslaw.substack.com/p/exclusive-government-spy-hubs-are.

I request the following records created, received, or shared by this center from January 1, 2026 through the date this request is processed:

1. Any intelligence bulletin containing the term "Flock" or "DeFlock" (case-insensitive); and
2. Any communication containing the term "Flock" or "DeFlock" (case-insensitive).

For purposes of this request, "communications" includes email, text messages, chat or direct messages on collaboration platforms, memoranda, and correspondence, including attachments.

If portions of responsive records are exempt from disclosure, please redact only those portions and produce all reasonably segregable non-exempt material. If any records are withheld in whole or in part, please identify each withheld record, the statutory exemption relied upon, and the basis for withholding.

These records will be used in reporting for 404 Media, an independent technology-journalism outlet (https://www.404media.co/). The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for a commercial purpose.

I request that responsive records be provided electronically whenever possible. If fees are anticipated, please inform me of the total charges before fulfilling the request.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Koebler

***This email is being sent on behalf of Deputy Director Kristi Laughlin, SD-LECC Privacy Officer.***

To whom it may concern / MuckRock News / Jason Koebler,

The SD-LECC is in receipt of your request dated and received on August 11, 2026, requesting records pursuant to the California Public Records Act (CPRA).

Preliminarily, it must be stated that the SD-LECC is not a "public agency" within the meaning of the California Public Records Act.  It is a work location staffed with personnel from multiple local, state, and federal agencies working towards common operating goals, akin to a law enforcement "task force."  While a task force may, under certain circumstances, be considered a "public agency" within the meaning of the California Public Records Act and the Brown Act, those circumstances do not exist with regard to the SD-LECC.  Nevertheless, the SD-LECC, in the spirit of public disclosure and openness, is responding to the request as if the SD-LECC were a self-contained, distinct public agency.

In response to the request,  the SD-LECC is currently able to provide the attached records.

Response:
The SD-LECC has identified the documents listed below as responsive to your request.  After a careful review of each document the SD-LECC is providing the following response for each document.

Document: CIS Special Events – Emerging Risk Update – 07.15.2026 Originating Agency: CIS Center for Internet Security
Response: Pursuant to California Government Code § 7922.000, the SD‑LECC is withholding this document in its entirety. This document contains sensitive security-related information concerning potential threats, vulnerabilities, and situational awareness associated special events. Disclosure of this information could compromise security preparedness, expose potential vulnerabilities , or increase risks to public safety. Based on the specific security sensitive contents of the record, the public interest in protecting public safety and security operations clearly outweighs the public interest in disclosure.

Document: CIDG April 16 2026 meeting slides. Originating Agency: Critical Infrastructure Defense Group.
Response: This record is being withheld in full pursuant to Government Code §§ 7923.600 and 7927.705, and 6 U.S.C. § 482. The record contains law enforcement intelligence and critical infrastructure/homeland security information, including threat assessments, vulnerability information, and protective security information. Disclosure could reveal sensitive intelligence, security vulnerabilities, or protective measures related to public safety and critical infrastructure


Document: MS-ISAC PSTA Joint Study – Public Safety Agencies Face More Dynamic Cyber Threats – TLP GREEN. Originating Agency: Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center (MS-ISAC)

Response: This record is being withheld pursuant to Gov. Code §§ 7923.600 and 7927.705, and 6 U.S.C. § 482, because it contains cyber threat intelligence, critical infrastructure security information, and homeland security-related information, the disclosure of which could increase risks to public safety and protected infrastructure.



Document: NIAC Weekly Summary 01082026 Originating Agency: Nebraska Information Analysis Center Weekly Summary.

Response: This record is being withheld pursuant to GC 7923.600 which exempts law enforcement intelligence information from disclosure. Additionally, under GC 7922.000, a public agency may withhold a record if the public interest served by not disclosing the record clearly outweighs the public interest served by its disclosure.



Document: NIAC Weekly Summary 01222026 Originating Agency: Nebraska Information Analysis Center Weekly Summary.

Response: This record is being withheld pursuant to GC 7923.600 which exempts law enforcement intelligence information from disclosure. communications.subject: Maine Freedom of Access Act Request: Child care provider data
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maine Freedom of Access Act, I hereby request the following records:

Historical data on all licensed child care providers (active and closed) from as far back as data systems will allow to present. I also request data on license-exempt providers, if available. Specifically, I request the following information as it is available:

1) Provider ID
2) Provider name
3) Provider employer identification number (EIN) for nonprofit providers, if available
4) Provider employer identification number (EIN) for for-profit providers, if available
5) Street number
6) Street name
7) City
8) Zip code
9) Licensed capacity for each year (by child age group if available)
10) Enrollment for each year (by child age group if available)
11) Provider type (e.g., center-based provider, home-based provider, Head Start, school-based pre-K, etc.) for each year
12) First license issue (open) date
13) Most recent license issue date
14) Most recent license expiration date or close date
15) Ages served for each year
16) Hours of operation for each year
17) QRIS rating for each year (please explain who is required to participate and whether there are financial supports based on rating)
18) Accepts Child Care and Development Fund subsidies for each year
19) Accepts other types of subsidies for each year (please list types)
20) Prices for each year (by child age group if available)
21) Violation records

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by 1 M.R.S.A. § 408(6). The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Gabrielle Pepin

title: Public records regarding Pittsburg's community response & advisory committee

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Public records regarding Pittsburg's community response & advisory committee
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Government Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request copies of the following records. Where records exist in electronic form, I request them in their native electronic format (e.g., .msg/.eml for emails, .docx/.xlsx for documents and spreadsheets, and searchable PDF for scanned materials). I request that responsive records be produced on a rolling basis as they are identified, rather than withheld until all records have been compiled.

BACKGROUND

In November 2024, the Pittsburg City Council certified a Final Program Environmental Impact Report and adopted the Pittsburg Technology Park Specific Plan for a 76-acre campus on the former Delta View Golf Course, with the 92 MW "Perseus" data center proposed by AVAIO Digital Partners as its initial development. At its June 15, 2026 regular meeting, the Council received more than 100 public comments on the project; the City subsequently hosted a virtual community workshop on July 30, 2026, held a Special City Council Study Session on August 3, 2026, and on August 13, 2026 announced the formation of an Advisory Committee on Data Center Development. The City has also been named in litigation filed by the Center for Biological Diversity concerning the project's environmental review.

DEFINITIONS

"City" means the City of Pittsburg, including the City Council, City Manager's Office, City Attorney's Office, City Clerk, Community Development Department (including Planning and Economic Development), Public Works, the Water Department, and the Pittsburg Power Company, and any officer, employee, consultant, or agent acting on the City's behalf.

"Developer" means AVAIO Digital Partners, AVAIO Digital, AVAIO Capital, and any parent, subsidiary, affiliate, successor, consultant, attorney, lobbyist, or other representative acting on their behalf in connection with the Project, including but not limited to John DeLacio and Mark McComiskey.

"Project" means the Pittsburg Technology Park Specific Plan, the Perseus Data Center, and any other data center, "technology center," or "technology park" use proposed or approved on the former Delta View Golf Course site, including associated power, water, recycled water, or interconnection infrastructure.

"Communications" means emails and attachments, letters, memoranda, text messages, messages sent through any messaging platform, calendar invitations, and meeting notes, whether sent from or received on City-issued or personal accounts or devices, to the extent they concern the conduct of the public's business (City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608).

I am not requesting records already posted on the City's agenda portal or Project webpage (e.g., the Draft and Final Program EIR, adopted resolutions and ordinances, published agenda packets, and posted meeting videos). If a responsive record is publicly posted, a URL is sufficient.

REQUESTED RECORDS

1. Advisory Committee on Data Center Development; Formation and Selection Process

Public statements indicate that as of August 13, 2026, the City announced its intent to form an Advisory Committee on Data Center Development, but that the Committee had not yet been formed or its members appointed as of the date of this request. I request all records concerning the Committee's planning, design, and formation, including:

(a) any draft or final charter, scope, charge, bylaws, or terms of reference for the Committee;
(b) any draft or final eligibility or selection criteria for Committee membership;
(c) any application, nomination, or expression-of-interest form or template, whether or not yet released to the public, and any instructions or outreach materials describing how members of the public may apply, be nominated, or be selected;
(d) any list, tracking sheet, or record of individuals who have applied, been nominated, or been considered for Committee membership, with personal contact information redacted;
(e) any internal staff report, memorandum, presentation, or Communication discussing the Committee's purpose, authority (including whether its recommendations are binding on the City Council, the City Manager, or any other body), anticipated meeting schedule, or duration;
(f) any Communication discussing the timeline for forming the Committee, including any delay relative to the timeline announced on August 13, 2026, and the reasons for any such delay; and
(g) to the extent the Committee has been formed or its members appointed as of the date this request is processed, records reflecting the individuals appointed and their stated affiliations, and the agendas, materials, minutes, and recordings of any Committee meeting held to date.

2. July 30, 2026 Virtual Community Workshop

(a) All questions submitted in advance of or during the workshop, including via datacenters@pittsburgca.gov, the Zoom Q&A or chat function, or any online form, and any compilation, categorization, tally, or staff analysis of those questions;
(b) all presentation materials, slide decks, speaker notes, scripts, talking points, and briefing memoranda prepared for the workshop; and
(c) the complete recording of the workshop, including chat and Q&A logs, if not already posted.

3. Council Briefing Materials

All presentation materials, speaker notes, talking points, briefing memoranda, and prepared statements provided to or prepared for Council members for the June 15, 2026 regular meeting and the August 3, 2026 Special Study Session concerning the Project, including any staff-prepared responses to anticipated questions and any materials prepared by the Developer and distributed to Council or staff.

4. Overflow-Room Recording

Any audio or video recording of the overflow room used for the August 3, 2026 Special Study Session, if separate from the posted chamber recording.

5. Conflict-of-Interest and Recusal Records

All records from January 1, 2025 to present concerning any actual or potential conflict of interest of any Council member or Pittsburg Power Company board member with respect to the Project, including any request for advice submitted to the Fair Political Practices Commission, any advice letter or informal assistance received from the Commission, and any Communication from the City Attorney to a Council member regarding recusal from any Project-related item.

6. Public Correspondence Tally

Any log, spreadsheet, or tally maintained by the City Clerk, City Manager's Office, or Council staff of public comments, emails, letters, or calls received concerning the Project from June 1, 2026 to present. (I am requesting the log or summary only in this request; the underlying correspondence is the subject of a separate request.)

7. Public Records Request Log

Any log, tracking spreadsheet, or database export maintained by the City Clerk's office reflecting Public Records Act requests received concerning the Project from January 1, 2026 to present, including request date, a general description of the request, and its status or closure basis (e.g., "no responsive records," "produced," "denied"). Requester personal contact information may be redacted, but I request that any requester-stated organizational affiliation not be redacted.

I request that responsive records be produced on a rolling basis as they are identified, rather than withheld until all records have been compiled.

BACKGROUND

In November 2024, the Pittsburg City Council certified a Final Program Environmental Impact Report and adopted the Pittsburg Technology Park Specific Plan for a 76-acre campus on the former Delta View Golf Course, with the 92 MW "Perseus" data center proposed by AVAIO Digital Partners as its initial development. At its June 15, 2026 regular meeting, the Council received more than 100 public comments on the project; the City subsequently hosted a virtual community workshop on July 30, 2026, held a Special City Council Study Session on August 3, 2026, and on August 13, 2026 announced the formation of an Advisory Committee on Data Center Development. The City has also been named in litigation filed by the Center for Biological Diversity concerning the project's environmental review.

DEFINITIONS

"City" means the City of Pittsburg, including the City Council, City Manager's Office, City Attorney's Office, City Clerk, Community Development Department (including Planning and Economic Development), Public Works, the Water Department, and the Pittsburg Power Company, and any officer, employee, consultant, or agent acting on the City's behalf.

"Developer" means AVAIO Digital Partners, AVAIO Digital, AVAIO Capital, and any parent, subsidiary, affiliate, successor, consultant, attorney, lobbyist, or other representative acting on their behalf in connection with the Project, including but not limited to John DeLacio and Mark McComiskey.

"Project" means the Pittsburg Technology Park Specific Plan, the Perseus Data Center, and any other data center, "technology center," or "technology park" use proposed or approved on the former Delta View Golf Course site, including associated power, water, recycled water, or interconnection infrastructure.

"Communications" means emails and attachments, letters, memoranda, text messages, messages sent through any messaging platform, calendar invitations, and meeting notes, whether sent from or received on City-issued or personal accounts or devices, to the extent they concern the conduct of the public's business (City of San Jose v. Superior Court (2017) 2 Cal.5th 608).

I am not requesting records already posted on the City's agenda portal or Project webpage (e.g., the Draft and Final Program EIR, adopted resolutions and ordinances, published agenda packets, and posted meeting videos). If a responsive record is publicly posted, a URL is sufficient.

I request all records concerning the Committee's planning, design, and formation, including:

(a) any draft or final charter, scope, charge, bylaws, or terms of reference for the Committee;
(b) any draft or final eligibility or selection criteria for Committee membership;
(c) any application, nomination, or expression-of-interest form or template, whether or not yet released to the public, and any instructions or outreach materials describing how members of the public may apply, be nominated, or be selected;
(d) any list, tracking sheet, or record of individuals who have applied, been nominated, or been considered for Committee membership, with personal contact information redacted;
(e) any internal staff report, memorandum, presentation, or Communication discussing the Committee's purpose, authority (including whether its recommendations are binding on the City Council, the City Manager, or any other body), anticipated meeting schedule, or duration;
(f) any Communication discussing the timeline for forming the Committee, including any delay relative to the timeline announced on August 13, 2026, and the reasons for any such delay; and
(g) to the extent the Committee has been formed or its members appointed as of the date this request is processed, records reflecting the individuals appointed and their stated affiliations, and the agendas, materials, minutes, and recordings of any Committee meeting held to date.

(c) the complete recording of the workshop, including chat and Q&A logs, if not already posted.

All presentation materials, speaker notes, talking points, briefing memoranda, and prepared statements provided to or prepared for Council members for the June 15, 2026 regular meeting and the August 3, 2026 Special Study Session concerning the Project, including any staff-prepared responses to anticipated questions and any materials prepared by the Developer and distributed to Council or staff.

4. Overflow-Room Recording

Any audio or video recording of the overflow room used for the August 3, 2026 Special Study Session, if separate from the posted chamber recording.

5. Conflict-of-Interest and Recusal Records

All records from January 1, 2025 to present concerning any actual or potential conflict of interest of any Council member or Pittsburg Power Company board member with respect to the Project, including any request for advice submitted to the Fair Political Practices Commission, any advice letter or informal assistance received from the Commission, and any Communication from the City Attorney to a Council member regarding recusal from any Project-related item.

Any log, spreadsheet, or tally maintained by the City Clerk, City Manager's Office, or Council staff of public comments, emails, letters, or calls received concerning the Project from June 1, 2026 to present. (I am requesting the log or summary only in this request; the underlying correspondence is the subject of a separate request.)

7. Public Records Request Log

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Tahoma School District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: FW: Maine Freedom of Access Act Request: slic
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Petti:
I am in receipt of your request for information sent on October 14, 2026.

The Maine Freedom of Access Act defines public records as those that are "in the possession or custody of an agency or public official of this State" and "received or prepared for use in connection with the transaction of public or governmental business or contain[] information relating to the transaction of public or governmental business . . . ." 1 MRSA §402(3). The definition excludes certain records that meet the requirements of Title 1, section 402, subsection 3, paragraphs A-V, as well as any records that are designated confidential by statute. The Act does not require creation of a record that does not exist. 1 MRSA §408-A(6).  Compiling the public record includes searching for, reviewing, and redacting confidential information, and the Act authorizes agencies to charge a fee in the amount of $25 per hour after the first two hours of staff time to cover the actual cost of searching for, retrieving, and compiling requested records.

As I understand your request, you are seeking the following public records:

Regarding Senator Trey Stewart:  (please note that, contrary to the language in your request, Sen. Stewart is the Senate Minority Leader, not the President of the Senate)
·      Emails sent from January 1, 2025 and October 14, 2026 between any email address ending in  "@statelegislatorisraelcaucus.com" and Sen. Trey Stewart, or his staff in the Senate Republican Office.
·      Emails sent from January 1, 2025 and October 14, 2026 between any email address ending in "@gov.il" and Sen. Trey Stewart or his staff in the Senate Republican Office that include the any of the following terms:

     *   "State Legislators Israel Caucus";
     *   "SLIC";
     *   "50 States, One Israel"; or
     *   "50 States, One Nation".
  *   Any calendar entries, meeting invitations, and scheduling records for Senator Trey Stewart concerning the State Legislators Israel Caucus (SLIC) or the "50 States, One Israel" / "50 States, One Nation" conference;
  *   Any records of travel, lodging, or expenses paid for, reimbursed to, or arranged for Senator Trey Stewart in connection with the State Legislators Israel Caucus (SLIC) or the "50 States, One Israel" conference, including reimbursement forms, expense reports, and travel or gift disclosures;
  *   Records identifying the source of funding for the participation of Senator Trey Stewart in the State Legislators Israel Caucus (SLIC) or the "50 States, One Israel" conference.
Regarding Representative Reagan Paul:
·      Emails sent from January 1, 2025 and October 14, 2026 between any email address ending in  "@statelegislatorisraelcaucus.com" and Rep. Reagan Paul, or her staff in the House Republican Office.
·      Emails sent from January 1, 2025 and October 14, 2026 between any email address ending in "@gov.il" and Rep. Reagan Paul or her staff in the House Republican Office that include the any of the following terms:

communications.communication:
Good afternoon Mr. Beckett –
Following a good faith search, please see the attached records responsive to your request available to the public. Records of the Denver Police Department are criminal justice records, the disclosure of which is governed by the Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act (CCJRA), sections 24-72-301, et. seq. C.R.S.  Except for records of “official actions,” the disclosure of criminal justice records is discretionary and can be denied where the custodian believes disclosure would be contrary to the public interest. Section 24-72-305(5), C.R.S.
 Pursuant to Harris v. Denver Post, 123 P.3d 116 (Colo. 2005), the following factors , in addition to other relevant considerations,  may be used to determine whether a record should be released or withheld:

  1.  the privacy interests of individuals, if any, who may be impacted by a decision to allow disclosure of the record;
  2.  the agency’s interest in keeping confidential information confidential;
  3.  the agency’s interest in the integrity of on-going investigations;
  4.  the public purpose to be served in allowing disclosure of the record; and
  5.  any other pertinent considerations relevant to the circumstances of the records request, including whether disclosure would be contrary to the public interest.
Based upon my consideration of the relevant factors, I have determined that certain information should be redacted from the report prior to public disclosure to protect privacy and interests which outweigh the public interest in disclosure of the information.  The redacted columns include, names of officers, case numbers, time frame, license plate information, search coordinates, vehicle description, filters (which included case numbers and other information related to criminal investigation)s) and entries from within the reason column have been redacted.
We also want to proactively share some important context with you regarding two entries in the May audit log.

The two queries on May 19, 2026, with the offense category listed as “Other; Immigration Violator” were test queries submitted by Denver Police personnel during DPD’s testing phase conducted prior to the go-live date of June 3, 2026, for its Axon ALPR pilot program. More specifically, the queries were submitted to see if the system would allow such a query and how it would be reported in the audit so that DPD could provide feedback to the vendor. So, to be clear, these two queries were submitted for the purpose of testing the system prior to implementation and were not submitted for the purpose of any enforcement.
In accordance with Denver municipal ordinance and Colorado law, the Denver Police Department does not assist with the enforcement of civil federal immigration laws.

Thank you,

Andrea

title: Arrest log fields and 30-day arrest log (Kent Police Department)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Arrest log fields and 30-day arrest log (Kent Police Department)
communications.communication:
Hello, and thank you for the work you do at the Kent Police Department.

I'm writing from the Records Desk at Tempo by Multido with a small public records request under the Washington Public Records Act (RCW 42.56). I know records staff are busy, so I've tried to keep this as simple as I can.

Could you please share:

1. A list of the fields your arrest records system keeps (for example: arrest number, arrest date, name, date of birth, charges, location, booking photo). A screenshot, a report header or a short description is perfectly fine.
2. The arrest log for the most recent 30 days, in whatever electronic form is easiest for you. A standard report export, a spreadsheet or a PDF all work.

I'd also love to know: does your office offer an email list, notification system or regular report (daily or weekly) that shares new bookings or arrests? If so, we'd be glad to sign up, so you wouldn't need to handle requests like this one in the future.

If any part is exempt, please feel free to send the rest. And if another office is the better place to ask, a quick pointer would be very much appreciated.

Thank you so much for your time and help. We really appreciate it.

Warmly,
Logan

Email metadata only (sender, all recipients including cc and bcc, subject line, and date and time; no message body or attachments) for any email to or from an address at axon.com, fusus.com, flocksafety.com, soundthinking.com, shotspotter.com, or ourmayors.org (the African American Mayors Association, AAMA) in the email accounts of Mayor Van R. Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

title: Jail booking fields and 30-day booking log (Morgan County Sheriff's Office)

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Jail booking fields and 30-day booking log (Morgan County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
Hello, and thank you for the work you do at the Morgan County Sheriff's Office.

I'm writing from the Records Desk at Tempo by Multido with a small public records request under the Colorado Open Records Act (CORA) and Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act (CCJRA). I know records staff are busy, so I've tried to keep this as simple as I can.

Could you please share:

1. A list of the fields your jail booking system keeps (for example: booking number, booking date, name, date of birth, charges, bond, release date, booking photo). A screenshot, a report header or a short description is perfectly fine.
2. The booking log for the most recent 30 days, in whatever electronic form is easiest for you. A standard report export, a spreadsheet or a PDF all work.

I'd also love to know: does your office offer an email list, notification system or regular report (daily or weekly) that shares new bookings or arrests? If so, we'd be glad to sign up, so you wouldn't need to handle requests like this one in the future.

If any part is exempt, please feel free to send the rest. And if another office is the better place to ask, a quick pointer would be very much appreciated.

Thank you so much for your time and help. We really appreciate it.

Warmly,
Logan

communications.communication:
Hello,
This email is a response to your CORA request to the Morgan County
Sheriff's Office dated November 10th, 2026.

The list of the fields we complete during a booking are listed below:
We assign a jacket number to the inmate if one is not assigned. This is a
number that follows the inmate anytime they are incarcerated with our
department.

We collect name, date of birth, social security number, address, height,
weight, eye color and hair color. We collect ethnicity, as well as place of
birth. We also list an emergency contact if one is available.

We enter arrest location and charges from what the officer provides us.

We take a mugshot of the inmate, front view and profile. We also document
scars, marks and tattoos by picture and written description.

We complete mental health screening questions, medical screening questions
and a suicide screening questionairre.

We also input court hearings and next court appearance dates as well as
sentence timeframes. We collect victim information on VRA crimes.

We are connected to the mobile patrol app which shows general information
on inmates.

Attached is a booking log for the most recent 30 days.

title: DoD/Dept. of War support for "Gold Star Growing Up - Service and a Legacy of War"

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: DoD/Dept. of War support for "Gold Star Growing Up - Service and a Legacy of War"
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents pertaining to collaboration between the Department of Defense (DoD)/Dept. of War and the production of "Gold Star Growing Up - Service and a Legacy of War." This title appears on a list of 2025 DoD/Dept. of War entertainment industry collaborations released to me through FOIA. The list is attached to this request. Requested documents may include but should not be limited to: script notes; production assistance agreements; photographs; and all records of communications between employees of DoD/Dept. of War and members of the cast, crew, and production company of "Gold Star Growing Up" including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication.

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation as well as the editor-in-chief and a contributor to a research magazine published by said foundation titled "Cultural Engineering Studies." These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Carollo

title: Itemized Fee Petitions, Invoices, and Settlement Payouts (McMinimee Law)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Itemized Fee Petitions, Invoices, and Settlement Payouts (McMinimee Law)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All itemized invoices, line-item billing sheets, and fee petitions submitted to the Wenatchee School District, its legal affairs department, or its risk-management carriers by Shannon McMinimee or any agent operating under the domain or entity name "McMinimee Law".
2. All transactional records, ledger entries, checks, or electronic funds transfer records documenting attorney fee payouts, cost reimbursements, or financial settlement distributions paid directly to McMinimee Law or Shannon McMinimee.
3. The chronological scope of this request spans from January 1, 2022, through June 3, 2025, specifically targeting all billing blocks and fee recovery actions generated while the attorney was concurrently operating under private credentials and public employment contracts.

PRE-EMPTIVE STATUTORY ENFORCEMENT & COMPLIANCE CLAUSE:
The District is advised that, per Washington law (Progressive Animal Welfare Soc. v. University of Wash.), attorney billing records for public payment are subject to disclosure. Only specific, narrow redactions (e.g., student names under FERPA) are permitted, as blanket privilege claims are invalid under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:
A response is expected within five business days as per RCW 42.56.520. The records, requested for non-commercial purposes, should be provided electronically.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kung Fu Joe

title: LexisNexis Emails and Invoices - MD (Takoma Park Police Department)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: LexisNexis Emails and Invoices - MD (Takoma Park Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All invoices you have received from LexisNexis from January 2026 through the date of fulfilment of this request. 

2) All emails between your agency and LexisNexis, from July 15 to the date of fulfilment of this request. 
- 2.a) Domains: all emails between your agency and "@lexisnexis.com", "@lexisnexisrisk.com", or "@lnssi.com". Timeframe: March 24, 2026 through September 24, 2026.
- 2.b) Include: emails, attachments, inline and embedded images, links, and the subject and to/from/cc lines. Please provide the original emails in full.
- 2.c) Exclude: Duplicates and mass-mailings may be de-duplicated so that only a single representative example is produced. If your agency receives automated, repeating status or upload-confirmation messages, please include a sample of three rather than the full set. Automated password reset and account notification emails may be excluded.
- 2.d) Format: if possible, please provide the original electronic files (.eml, .msg, .mbox, .pst, or a similar native format) so the integrity of the original messages is preserved. 
- 2.e) If any emails are withheld in whole or in part, please include a list of what was withheld and cite the specific exemption relied on for each.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: 2026 Code Violations
